summary: CodeGrep is a 14B model trained with GRPO to run multi-turn grep/glob/read calls and return a few candidate files. Its training labels are mined from 67K public OpenHands trajectories. The candidates are injected into the prompt of a frozen OpenHands agent running Qwen3-30B-A3B. On SWE-Bench Verified the resolve rate moves from 25.8% to 27.0% (single run), with 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens on resolved issues. Injecting BM25 candidates instead made the agent slower and slightly worse.

claims.claim: CodeGrep lifts SWE-Bench Verified resolve rate by +1.2 pp (25.8%→27.0%), 'small but reproducibly positive'
claims.evidence: Table 3: 129→135 of 500 resolved, a single temperature-0 run per configuration; no seeds or CIs. 'Reproducibly' rests on v1 and v3 both hitting 27.0%, which are different models.

claims.claim: CodeGrep cuts rounds 15% and tokens 19% on resolved instances
claims.evidence: Table 3 pooled over each config's own resolved set; §5.3 paired restriction to 96 jointly resolved instances shrinks this to −9% rounds and −15% tokens. Authors report the selection effect themselves.

claims.claim: Downstream utility follows a precision threshold: low-precision injection hurts, mid is neutral, high buys efficiency
claims.evidence: Tables 2-3: BM25 precision 0.375 → −0.6 pp and +21% tokens (+38.6% on 94 paired instances); Jina 0.445 → neutral; CodeGrep 0.677 → −19% tokens. Three retrievers, one downstream agent, one run each. 'Threshold' is a three-point monotone trend, not a located threshold.

claims.claim: Applying the efficiency signal at the GRPO advantage layer rather than the reward layer cuts KL drift to one-third
claims.evidence: §5.2, Fig. 2b: KL ~0.31 vs ~0.09 across one training run each; v2 then shows length exploitation.

patterns.note: A learned agent issuing grep/glob/read beats BM25 and a dense retriever on file precision; injecting BM25 candidates hurts the downstream agent. Lexical tools work when an agent drives them, while lexical ranking used as a one-shot hint does not.
Jina-1.5B dense retrieval injection is roughly neutral downstream.
A separate exploration model whose only output is a short file list compresses the downstream agent's exploration; the effect is on cost, not on resolve rate.
GRPO reward-design iterations for a retrieval agent; single run per variant.

methodology.sample: SWE-Bench Verified 500; internal retrieval set from held-out swe-rebench instances (size not stated) with CATM labels audited by the authors' engineers
methodology.baselines: No retrieval, BM25 top-2, Jina-1.5B top-2; no comparison to Agentless/Moatless localization or SWE-grep
methodology.variance: None; single run per configuration (baseline matches public 25.2±0.7)
methodology.contamination_controls: Training labels from public OpenHands trajectories that may cover SWE-bench-like repos; no overlap check reported

standards.artifacts: Model, pipeline, environment and harnesses 'will be released'; not yet

biases.detail: +1.2 pp = 6 instances out of 500 on one run; the baseline's own published std is 0.7 pp.
One downstream agent (Qwen3-30B-A3B); whether the threshold transfers is stated as open.
CATM mines OpenHands trajectories on public GitHub repos; overlap with SWE-Bench Verified repos is not checked.
'Reproducibly positive' for a single-run 1.2 pp delta.

coi.affiliations: NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab; independent researchers
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None of NetEase's products; Qwen and Jina models used
coi.detail: Industry lab, but no own product is evaluated favorably.

verdict_reason: Honest about the efficiency-over-effectiveness result and the pooled-vs-paired selection effect. The resolve lift is within noise, and there is one downstream agent, one language and no variance.
applicability: The transferable point for a Java team is not the trained model, which is Python-only, unreleased, and paired with a weak downstream agent. It is the injection caution: pre-seeding an agent's prompt with low-precision candidate files (BM25-grade) costs tokens and can lower success. Any code-graph or index tool that pushes candidates into context should be precision-checked. It does not show a small explorer serving a frontier solver: the solver is a 30B-A3B model at 25.8%.

conflicts_with.detail: That paper finds eager dense candidates beat eager BM25 on repair; CodeGrep agrees on ordering but finds dense injection only neutral downstream, with gains appearing only at higher precision.
